issues.issue: Initial transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous is triggered by 'Power On', but per spec, Power On should transition the system INTO HumanDriving mode (from initial/off state), not out of it.
issues.reason: Spec item 3 states 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode', meaning Power On should be the trigger for entering HumanDriving (e.g., from [*] or an off state), not a trigger for leaving HumanDriving into Autonomous.

issues.issue: There is no explicit transition guarded by Power On leading into HumanDriving; the only incoming edge to HumanDriving from [*] is unconditional.
issues.reason: Spec item 3 explicitly ties entering HumanDriving mode to the 'power on' event. The model's initial transition lacks this trigger, so the causal link between Power On and entering HumanDriving is missing.

issues.issue: Transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous is guarded by 'Front Distance > 10', duplicating/conflicting with the Power-On-labeled transition already present between the same two states.
issues.reason: Having two transitions between the same states with different, unrelated guards (Power On vs Front Distance > 10) is inconsistent with the spec, which specifies only one condition (front_distance > 10) for auto-transport into autonomous state (item 4). The Power On labeled transition here is a mislabeling/duplication error.
issues.where: Transitions: HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On AND HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10

issues.issue: The composite/submachine state 'Autonomous' is modeled as also being a normal state with its own outgoing transition to AutonomousIdle guarded by 'Front Distance <= 10', but the spec does not mention this condition or an Idle/Active split triggered by front distance in this way.
issues.reason: Spec item 4 only says: 'when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state' as the entry condition into Autonomous, and does not specify an internal Idle/Active sub-state distinction based on this same condition; the model introduces internal complexity and reuses the same guard confusingly, contradicting the simpler entry condition intended by the spec.
issues.where: State: Autonomous, transitions Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10, AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10

issues.issue: The transition to HumanDriving from Autonomous's final state ('in (auto final)') is missing.
issues.reason: Spec item 4 explicitly lists three conditions for transiting back to human driving mode: 'human steering cmd', 'brake pressed', and 'in (auto final)'. The model only implements the first two (from AutonomousActive) but never transitions from AutonomousFinal back to HumanDriving.

issues.issue: AutonomousActive has no transition into AutonomousFinal, so the submachine's final state is unreachable.
issues.reason: For the 'in (auto final)' condition in spec item 4 to ever be meaningful, the submachine must be able to reach its final state. Since no transition leads to AutonomousFinal, this exit condition can never trigger, making the state machine incomplete relative to the spec.

issues.issue: Power Off transition originates only from HumanDriving, not from any Autonomous sub-state.
issues.reason: Spec item 5 states 'when power off, it will transit to final state' without restricting this to only the human driving mode; the system should presumably support powering off from any active state (including Autonomous states), but the model only allows Power Off from HumanDriving.

issues.issue: The final state used for Power Off is named 'AutonomousFinal' and annotated as 'Auto Final State', conflating the overall system's final state with the autonomous submachine's final state.
issues.reason: The spec distinguishes between the overall system final state (item 5, on power off) and the autonomous submachine's final state (item 4, 'auto final'). The model conflates these into a single state, which misrepresents the specification's intent of two distinct final states serving different purposes.
issues.where: State: AutonomousFinal used both as target for 'Power Off' and implied as the submachine exit state referenced in spec item 4 ('in (auto final)')

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On
Autonomous : Autonomous Mode
Autonomous : <<submachine>>

Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10
AutonomousIdle : Autonomous Idle Mode

AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10
AutonomousActive : Autonomous Active Mode

AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Human Steering Cmd
AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Brake Pressed

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10
HumanDriving --> AutonomousFinal : Power Off

AutonomousFinal : Auto Final State
@enduml
